2025-11.daily_overview: After recovering from her lumbar injury, Song Yajing used her newly bought folding electric scooter for the first time to go to the clothing wholesale market, efficiently replenishing the shop's winter accessories and new styles. In the afternoon, she sorted inventory and estimated sales for the next day's Double 11 Kuaituantuan and livestream joint event, and posted a preview in the community group. In the evening, she went to the supermarket to buy core ingredients for the Mediterranean diet and cooked the first day of experimental healthy meals for the family. However, a problem arose at dinner—Zhiqiang protested that "there is no rice," and Xuanxuan flatly refused to eat chickpeas, leading to a small table negotiation between mother and daughter. Late at night, she received the medical insurance settlement statement for her mother's hospitalization, confirmed the out-of-pocket portion, and called her sister to discuss how to share the costs.

events.name: Use an electric scooter to go to the wholesale market to purchase new styles.
events.description: In the morning, mindful that her lower back still needed protection and she couldn't walk long distances with heavy loads, Song Yajing dug out the foldable electric scooter she had bought last month from the storage room. After charging it and putting on a helmet, she rode along Siming South Road all the way to a clothing wholesale market in Huli District. She wove through familiar fabric, accessory, and ready-made garment stalls, and with her years of keen eye, quickly picked out several cable-knit sweaters popular this year, corduroy wide-leg pants, and a few designer scarves and hats. In the afternoon, Xiaomei would come to take over and bring the goods back to the store for inventory. Efficient and free—she enjoyed the exhilarating feeling of the wind rushing through her hair during the commute, and thought to herself: I'll use this for short-distance stocking trips from now on.

events.name: Preparing inventory and community engagement for the Double 11 event.
events.description: After returning from the wholesale market, Song Yajing carefully checked the inventory in the store's backend system and made final preparations for the Double 11 Kuaituantuan and livestream campaign that would start the next day. She estimated likely sales for each style, moved some popular basic items from the back of the inventory to a centralized area convenient for picking, and went over the try-on order and talking points for the livestream with Xiaomei. At 3 p.m., she posted the Double 11 preview poster and the Kuaituantuan opening notice in the WeChat customer community of more than 200 people, announcing a WeChat Channels livestream try-on at 7 p.m. the next evening.

events.name: Purchased Mediterranean diet ingredients, prepared three meals, and recorded her impressions.
events.description: In the evening, Song Yajing rode her scooter to the Yonghui Supermarket near her home and bought the core ingredients of the Mediterranean diet according to the list she had made the day before: a bottle of extra virgin olive oil, fresh salmon fillets, chicken breast, canned chickpeas, quinoa, whole-wheat toast, Greek yogurt, mixed lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, and various fruits. She happily filled her shopping cart, thinking this was an investment in the whole family's health. After returning home, she tied on an apron and strictly followed the recipe downloaded from the internet: for breakfast she made Greek yogurt with blueberries and walnuts (noting that she had already eaten it early in the morning); lunch was a takeout salad from the convenience store; for dinner she carefully cooked pan-seared salmon steaks and chickpea salad with tomato and cucumber cubes, with whole-wheat bread as the staple (for herself and Zhiqiang) and quinoa rice (for Xuanxuan to try). She seriously wrote in her notebook: "Day one impressions: during cooking there was less oil smoke, and the fish was easy to pan-fry. But—when Zhiqiang saw there was no plain white rice on the table, his expression looked like someone owed him money; Xuanxuan poked the chickpeas with her fork and asked, 'Is this rabbit food?' I patiently explained that this was a new way of eating and good for health, and she forced one bite and then spit it out." Her husband protested: "We Minnan people won't have any strength if we don't eat rice! This is like a monk eating a vegetarian diet." Song Yajing smiled and reassured him: "Just one week, let's try it." Although the dinner atmosphere had a hint of protest, she insisted on completing the day's meals according to the plan.

events.name: Received my mother's medical insurance settlement statement and discussed the cost sharing with my elder sister.
events.description: At eight in the evening, Song Yajing received a photo sent by her father via WeChat — the medical insurance settlement statement for her mother Lin Xiuying's current hospitalization. She carefully checked the details and confirmed that after insurance reimbursement, the out-of-pocket portion totaled exactly 8,000 yuan. She forwarded the photo to her older sister Song Yawen and then made a phone call. After a brief discussion, the two sisters agreed to each bear 50%, that is, 4,000 yuan each. Yawen said she was too busy with work recently to come home and visit, and Yajing said she understood and that she would transfer the money tomorrow.

2025-11.daily_overview: On Double 11 (Singles' Day), the store held its annual promotion. In the morning, the winter new-arrival package from Guangzhou arrived at the store on time. Song Yajing checked it carefully and entered it into the system. From afternoon to evening, she and Xiaomei hosted livestream sales on WeChat Channels in the store, while simultaneously launching group-buying events on Kuaituantuan. However, because her earlier inventory forecasts for several popular dresses and cardigans had been too conservative, the items sold out less than an hour after the livestream began. As a result, some customers who had already paid could not receive their goods on time, and scattered complaints and negative reviews began to appear in the community group. As for meals, she continued with the second day of the Mediterranean diet, cooking breakfast with olive oil and preparing grilled fish with vegetable salad for lunch. That night, however, she had insomnia after receiving several negative-review notifications late at night, and began to reflect on her inventory strategy.

events.name: Receive new winter arrivals and complete warehousing
events.description: At ten in the morning, the large parcel from Guangzhou was delivered to the store by the courier company on time. Song Yajing and Xiaomei carried the cartons into the warehouse and opened them one by one for checking. Wearing reading glasses (which she didn't actually need, just used as a prop to appear careful), she carefully checked every garment's style, color, size, and quantity against the order details. She hung the cable-knit sweaters and camel-colored coats on the display rack and neatly folded the scarves. After confirming there were no errors, she entered all the newly arrived inventory into the inventory management app, making ample preparations for selecting items for tonight's livestream.

events.name: Livestream sales in conjunction with Kuaituantuan, and popular styles quickly sold out.
events.description: At five in the afternoon, Song Yajing and Xiaomei set up the fill light and phone tripod in the small compartment behind the shop and started the Double 11 special livestream. Xiaomei was in charge of trying on the clothes and showing details, while Song Yajing explained the fabrics, styling, and discount rules beside her. A Kuaituantuan link was displayed below the livestream screen, so customers could order directly in the mini program. Thanks to thorough community warm-up and some traffic recommendation from the WeChat Channels platform, the number of simultaneous online viewers once reached over 200. Among them, a French floral-print dress was immediately sold out as soon as the group-buy opened. However, because Song Yajing had stocked up based on her experience in line with the traditional inventory quantity, she had only prepared 20 pieces of each of these two styles. In less than an hour, the inventory was cleared, and the continued influx of subsequent orders faced a situation where there was no stock to ship.

events.name: Received negative reviews and complaints due to insufficient stock
events.description: After the livestream ended, Song Yajing opened the Kuaituantuan backend and found more than 30 pending orders, but several best-selling items were out of stock and could not be fulfilled. At the same time, negative comments appeared in the WeChat customer community. A regular customer tagged her: "@Shopkeeper Yajing, I clearly grabbed that floral dress, so why do I see people in the group saying it's out of stock? This Singles' Day is so unreliable!" Then two or three similar questions followed, accompanied by frustrated or angry emojis. Song Yajing's heart sank, knowing that she had made a mistake by being too conservative in her inventory estimate. She immediately responded in the group: "I'm very sorry. This is indeed a problem caused by insufficient stock. I am contacting affected customers one by one and will definitely provide a compensation plan." Afterwards, she received a formal negative review that read: "After I placed the order, they told me it was out of stock. I got my hopes up for nothing." She read that line three times and took a deep breath.

events.name: Day 2 of continuing the Mediterranean diet, trying cooking with less oil
events.description: Despite the busy shop schedule, Song Yajing insisted on following the plan for the second day of the Mediterranean diet experiment. In the morning she made a vegetable omelet with olive oil for breakfast. At noon she had Xiaomei pick up grilled fish fillet and a plain vegetable salad from a nearby restaurant, and she skipped rice. For dinner she quickly cooked whole-wheat pasta with homemade tomato sauce and shrimp, and deliberately replaced the corn oil she used for stir-frying with olive oil, cutting the amount to half of what she usually used. Her husband Chen Zhiqiang saw 'whole wheat' on the table again, sighed, but did not protest again. Song Yajing quietly added an extra spoonful of tomato sauce to his plate as a consolation.

events.name: Late-night insomnia reflection on stocking strategy.
events.description: At 11 p.m. deep in the night, her daughter and husband were both sound asleep. Song Yajing, however, lay with her eyes open staring at the ceiling, replaying in her mind the scene of products being snapped up during the livestream and those negative reviews. She let out a soft sigh, reached for her phone on the nightstand, opened her memo, and typed a few lines: "Lesson: 1. Conservative stocking in the livestream = driving customers away; 2. The impulse buying wasn't me being impulsive; it was my forecasting mistake; 3. Before the next livestream, I must refer to the community pre-order data and not rely entirely on old experience." She benchmarked herself from a "small shop owner" to a "professional buyer," realizing that this setback was actually tuition for professional growth.

2025-11.daily_overview: The lesson from Double 11 needed to be made up for as soon as possible. In the morning, Song Yajing publicly issued a sincere apology in the community, admitted that she had miscalculated her inventory preparation, and offered free shipping and handwritten thank-you cards as compensation for affected customers. In her management notes, she wrote down her reflections and treated the lesson as an opportunity to grow from 'buying on gut feeling' to becoming a 'data-driven buyer.' As for her diet, she had persisted into the third day, but inside she had already begun to strongly miss the satay noodles from her hometown. In the evening, she could no longer suppress the craving. She cooked a steaming bowl of satay noodles and enjoyed it alone—the Mediterranean diet plan was declared suspended on the evening of the third day with a bowl of satay noodles. Late at night, news suddenly came in the high school class WeChat group that Wu Xiaoli's father had passed away from lung cancer. Grieving, Song Yajing immediately sent private messages to comfort her and began coordinating with classmates in Xiamen to express condolences together.

events.name: Publicly post an apology statement in the community and provide a compensation plan
events.description: At nine in the morning, Song Yajing composed a long message in the customer community of more than 200 people and pinned it as a group announcement. She wrote: “Dear sisters, this is Yajing. Regarding the problem last night during the Double 11 livestream where some styles were sold out and orders that had been paid for could not be shipped, I want to sincerely apologize to everyone here. I misjudged the demand for the event and did not stock enough, so you all waited for nothing. I am very, very sorry. As compensation, the affected sisters will enjoy free shipping on their next purchase at the store, no matter the amount, and I will include a handwritten thank-you card in every package. This is my heartfelt gesture, and also a lesson. Thank you for your understanding. I will work hard to do better.” After sending it, she put down her phone, covered her face with both hands, and let out a long sigh. In the group, people gradually replied with “Understand” and “Keep going, Yajing,” and the regular customer who had complained earlier also sent a hug emoji: “Okay, I understand you. Running a small shop isn’t easy.” Only then did she feel the weight on her shoulders ease a little.

events.name: Reflecting on the Double 11 experience, adjust the buying strategy.
events.description: After the apology statement was released, Song Yajing opened her store management notebook (a dark blue A5 ring binder) and carefully wrote down a reflection under the "Growth Notes" category: "Double 11 lesson - as a buyer, I need to shift from the intuitive stocking of 'I think this looks good' to the rational stocking of 'data shows this will sell.' Before the next big promotion, I must first run community polls, pre-orders, and inventory stress tests. Making mistakes is not scary; not correcting them is what's scary." She set this learning experience as a must-read entry before the December Christmas event, and decided to track the sales conversion rate of bestsellers and new items every week starting next week.

events.name: Third day of following the Mediterranean diet; a longing for hometown flavors is stirring.
events.description: Today was the third day of the Mediterranean diet experiment. For breakfast, Greek yogurt with fruit and nuts; for lunch, she had a nearby salad shop deliver hummus with whole-wheat flatbread and vegetable sticks. For dinner, she followed the recipe and made a Mediterranean-style fish stew—slow-cooked tomatoes, olives, and fish chunks, served with quinoa and roasted vegetables. When Chen Zhiqiang saw quinoa again, his expression went a bit blank. As for Song Yajing herself, halfway through the fish stew, an image of steaming hot shacha noodles uncontrollably rose in her mind—a rich shacha sauce broth, springy oil noodles, a few slices of pork neck marbled with fat and lean, and bright green bean sprouts. She forced herself to finish the fish, but somewhere inside she was silently crying out: I want to eat shacha noodles. After dinner, she couldn't help opening Dianping on her phone and browsing user reviews and photos of several nearby shacha noodle shops. She was unusually low.

events.name: Cooked satay noodles and enjoyed them alone, declaring the diet experiment suspended
events.description: At nine in the evening, the daughter was asleep and her husband was working overtime in the study. Song Yajing sat alone in the living room. After a small inner struggle, she finally got up and walked into the kitchen. She took out a bundle of oil noodles from the cupboard, and from the freezer, a pack of previously frozen satay soup base and a few slices of pork neck. About fifteen minutes later, a piping-hot bowl of Minnan satay noodles was in front of her. Without thinking, she picked up a mouthful of noodles and meat with her chopsticks and put it in her mouth; the rich satay sauce fragrance immediately filled her mouth. At that moment, she was almost moved to tears—this was not just food, it was her life memories and regional identity. Her husband smelled the aroma and came out. Seeing the messy leftover noodle bowl on the table, he said nothing, just shook his head with a helpless yet understanding smile. Daughter and husband had already eaten rice and stir-fried dishes at dinner, and had no interest in satay noodles. Song Yajing wiped her mouth, knowing clearly: the purely Western Mediterranean diet experiment was over, but the direction of healthy eating would not change. She needed to find a compromise between health and actual taste.

events.name: Learned that classmate Wu Xiaoli's father had passed away, and expressed condolences.
events.description: At 10:30 p.m., after washing up and getting ready for bed, Song Yajing habitually opened the WeChat high school classmates group chat. What caught her eye was a message that made her heart jolt—classmate Wu Xiaoli had posted an obituary: her father, whose advanced lung cancer had worsened a week earlier, had passed away peacefully this morning at their hometown in Quanzhou, and the funeral Mass was set for November 15 at a church in Quanzhou. Song Yajing's fingers froze, and Wu Xiaoli's face from high school surfaced in her mind. She immediately left the group chat and opened Wu Xiaoli's private message window. After thinking for a moment, she typed: 'Xiaoli, I just saw the news about Uncle. I'm so sad. I remember going to your house in high school, and Uncle cooked noodles for us. He was such a gentle man. Is there anything I can do? I want to pay my last respects to Uncle.' A few minutes later, Wu Xiaoli replied with a crying emoji and a message: 'Yajing, thank you. The Mass is on Saturday morning, the 15th, at our hometown in Quanzhou. If you can come, I'll feel at peace.' Song Yajing immediately replied: 'I'll definitely be there.'

events.name: Contact classmates in Xiamen to discuss jointly sending a funeral wreath, and ask her husband to look after their daughter.
events.description: After confirming she would attend the funeral Mass, Song Yajing contacted Li Meiling, who was also in Xiamen, and another high school classmate, Zhang Wei, via WeChat to discuss jointly paying for a funeral wreath. They quickly settled on the amount, and Zhang Wei contacted the flower shop. Then she walked to the study door, knocked lightly, and said to Chen Zhiqiang, who was clattering away at code: "Zhiqiang, on Saturday the 15th, I have to go to the funeral of my high school classmate Wu Xiaoli's father in Quanzhou. Can you take care of Xuanxuan for the whole day?" Chen Zhiqiang pushed up his glasses and asked with concern: "Are you sure you're okay?" Song Yajing nodded: "I'll drive there and back in one day. Xiaoli has helped me a lot — when my grandmother died in my freshman year of high school, she stayed with me while I cried. This time it's my turn to be there for her." Zhiqiang nodded: "Don't worry, leave Xuanxuan to me."

2025-11.daily_overview: After the Mediterranean diet experiment ended last night with a bowl of satay noodles, Song Yajing adjusted her strategy today, deciding to keep the healthy elements and adapt them to Minnan style. She continued cooking with olive oil and reduced the amount of oil, but restored familiar flavors to the family table. In the morning, she went to the supermarket to replenish ingredients and stopped by the bank to withdraw 4,000 yuan in cash and transfer it to her mother to help cover the out-of-pocket hospitalization expenses. While keeping accounts, she resolved to set aside a fixed monthly amount as a family medical emergency fund starting this month. In the afternoon, following the church visitation team's schedule, she went with fellow church member Aunt Lin Xiuying to visit elderly church members living alone, bringing fruit and homemade cake. In the evening, she continued posting the preview for the sale of the 'Mom's Recipe' booklet on November 14, and the touching story attracted a lot of attention.

events.name: Finalize the modified Southern Fujian diet plan that retains healthy elements.
events.description: At breakfast, Song Yajing, while making a vegetable omelet with eggs (using olive oil, lightly oiled), announced to Chen Zhiqiang, who was eating bread: "I've decided that from now on this family won't go fully Western Mediterranean. From today, the oil for stir-frying will be changed to olive oil or camellia oil, and the amount used will be one-third less than before; we'll eat sea fish or salmon two or three times a week; whole grains will be served to the extent that you all don't find them too hard to accept; but we'll still eat rice, still make soup, and occasionally treat ourselves to shacha noodles. Health isn't built in a day—take it gradually." When Chen Zhiqiang heard "we'll still eat rice," he visibly relaxed. Song Yajing did as she said; all three meals that day kept the Minnan flavor while following the principle of less oil and less salt.

events.name: Go to the supermarket to stock up on healthy ingredients
events.description: In the morning, Song Yajing rode her electric scooter to Yonghui Supermarket once again. She put a bottle of extra virgin olive oil, two fresh salmon fillets, dried chickpeas, and various fresh vegetables into the shopping cart. Passing by the condiment section, she hesitated for a moment. In the end, she did not buy the satay sauce packet, but decided to make a low-salt version from scratch. She thought: the sustainability of a healthy diet must be built on a foundation that does not depart from local flavors.

events.name: Sales brochure warm-up promotion
events.description: After returning from the supermarket, Song Yajing sat behind the checkout counter and wrote a WeChat Moments post and a community announcement. She uploaded a close-up photo of her mother's handwritten recipe and a sample image of the exquisite booklet she had made, with the caption: "I grew up eating Mom's cakes. Now that she is sick, I want to preserve her craft. Starting tomorrow, the handwritten recipe booklet 'Mom's Recipes, The Sweetness of Time' will be sold at the shop, and all proceeds will be donated to the Xiamen Elderly Foundation. These yellowed notes from 20 years ago—every page is the taste of home." After the post went out, the group responded enthusiastically, and many regular customers left messages like "Reserve a copy for me" and "I'll come pick it up tomorrow."

events.name: Withdraw and transfer the mother's share of the medical expenses
events.description: At noon, Song Yajing withdrew 4,000 yuan in cash from the store’s petty cash account, then transferred it to her mother Lin Xiuying’s bank card via the ICBC mobile app, with the memo “medical expense contribution.” After the transfer, she opened the family emergency ledger (an Excel spreadsheet) and recorded under the “Health Expenses” category: “11.13 Share of mother’s out-of-pocket hospitalization costs for cerebral infarction, 4,000 yuan.” Staring at the figure, she pondered for a moment and wrote a new decision in her notebook: “Starting this month, set aside 2,000 yuan from my income every month into the emergency medical reserve fund account as a buffer pool for the family’s future health risks.” This decision was soon formally confirmed and upgraded at the family financial meeting with her husband on the 18th.

events.name: Visited an elderly church member living alone with fellow church members
events.description: At two in the afternoon, Song Yajing, following the duty schedule of the church's charity visitation team, rode her e-bike to meet fellow church member Aunt Lin Xiuying, and together they went to visit an elderly church member who lived alone in the old town of Siming. They brought a bag of fresh fruit and a low-sugar sponge cake that Song Yajing had baked herself that morning. The elderly church member, nearly eighty, had trouble moving around but was in good spirits. She held Song Yajing's hand and told stories about studying at a church school on Gulangyu Island in her youth, and Song Yajing listened with a smile. When they left, the old woman tremblingly traced a cross on Song Yajing's forehead and said, "The Lord bless you and your mother." Song Yajing's eyes grew warm, and she leaned down to hug the frail old woman.

events.name: Received an encouraging private message from a regular customer.
events.description: In the evening, while browsing community messages, Song Yajing received a private message from a regular customer, Vivian. Vivian said: “Seeing your apology and compensation plan, I think you're really thoughtful. The coat I bought last time has been asked about by many people for the link. Keep going, Yajing, we support you!” Song Yajing was deeply moved and replied with a long message of thanks. This recognition from a customer reignited her confidence.

2025-11.daily_overview: Today was the official sale day for the booklet “Mom's Recipe, the Sweetness of Time”. Customers came to the store one after another specifically to buy it, both old and young, and many were moved by the story behind it. Song Yajing kept a separate record of every payment to ensure that all proceeds would be donated. For dinner, she set aside all work, left the store to Xiaomei, who was on the Saturday shift, and went out alone with her husband Chen Zhiqiang for a meal of Quanzhou cuisine—today was their monthly agreed-upon “couple-only day”. In the afternoon, she also continued her improved healthy diet, using olive oil to replace part of the cooking oil to stir-fry a dish, and invited the whole family to taste it. In the evening, after discussing with her husband, they decided that starting tomorrow, the whole family would adopt the habit of taking a walk after dinner.

events.name: The official recipe booklet is now for sale
events.description: On Saturday morning, a small blackboard was hung on the shop door that read, "Mom's Recipes, the Sweetness of Time — On Sale Today." The booklets were neatly stacked on a display stand next to the cash register, and the cover featured a reproduction of an old red-covered notebook that Song Yajing had specially designed. From 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., community regulars, passing tourists, and a few church friends kept coming into the shop. A gray-haired elderly woman put on her reading glasses and looked through it carefully, then said to Song Yajing, "Your mother's handwriting is really beautiful, just like the recipes I wrote when I was young. I'll buy it." Another customer said she couldn't find customer service and only wanted the recipe booklet, so Song Yajing made a few orders selling only the booklet. She recorded the sale of each booklet in a dedicated ledger and silently calculated the total donation amount in her mind.

events.name: Cook reduced-oil dishes with olive oil and invite the whole family to taste them.
events.description: Mid-afternoon, she went home to cook. There were fresh seasonal vegetables in the fridge, so she decided to make garlic stir-fried spinach. Following the revised diet plan, she reduced the amount of cooking oil she usually poured by one-third and replaced the blended oil entirely with extra-virgin olive oil. The stir-fried spinach came out bright green and fragrant with garlic. She put a small portion on a plate and first gave it to her husband, who was sitting on the sofa watching TV: “Try it, the low-oil version.” Chen Zhiqiang picked up a bite with his chopsticks, chewed, and said with slight surprise: “It doesn't taste that different.” Yajing smiled with satisfaction, turned, and went into her daughter's room to tell Xuanxuan about it. For dinner, she pan-seared salmon with a spinach and tomato salad. The family's dining atmosphere was much more relaxed than in the previous few days.

events.name: The couple went out to dinner alone and planned a family after-dinner walking habit.
events.description: At six in the evening, after giving Xiaomei instructions on closing the store in advance, Song Yajing returned home, changed into a dress, and walked with her husband Chen Zhiqiang to a nearby restaurant run by someone from Quanzhou. This was their monthly 'couple-only day' dinner. After they sat down, Zhiqiang ordered a table of Quanzhou specialties—Quanzhou rice dumplings, misua noodle soup, and fried vinegar pork. The two ate and chatted, in a rare relaxed mood. Song Yajing mentioned that the booklet was selling well, and added that today's stir-fried spinach had drawn no complaints from her husband. 'Zhiqiang,' she put down her chopsticks and said seriously, 'starting tomorrow, I want the whole family to go out for a half-hour walk after dinner every day. Mom and Dad have had strokes, my lower back is weak, you sit all day long, and Xuanxuan needs to be more active. Walking is the safest exercise.' Chen Zhiqiang nodded: 'The lakeside greenway behind the neighborhood has bright lights at night. I've been thinking of suggesting you walk there. I know the route well—it's about three kilometers around the lake from home, just about half an hour.' The two used the map on their phones to roughly plan the walking route and agreed to start the next day.

events.name: Mild lower back discomfort before bed; used a support brace and applied a hot compress
events.description: After returning home in the evening, Song Yajing felt some soreness in her lower back, probably from standing too long in the store during the day. She took out the electric heating back support belt Wang Jia had sent her, set it to low, and applied heat for twenty minutes while resting in the massage chair. Zhiqiang poured her a glass of warm water and reminded her to use a car cushion when driving to Quanzhou tomorrow. Song Yajing nodded and decided to wear a lightweight back support when working in the store from now on.

2025-11.daily_overview: This Saturday was a substitute rest day, filled with farewell, gratitude, and new habits. In the early morning, Song Yajing checked the car by herself, then drove along the Shenhai Expressway to Quanzhou to attend the funeral Mass for the father of her high school classmate Wu Xiaoli. Throughout the ceremony, she sat quietly in the back row, praying for the deceased. After the Mass, she gave Wu Xiaoli a long hug and accompanied her in sorting through the belongings, and she did not drive back to Xiamen until 2 p.m. On the way back, she pulled over to call her father in Quanzhou and remind him to take care of his health. Returning to Xiamen in the evening, after the family dinner she initiated the new ritual of a family walk for the first time. Her husband and daughter walked for half an hour along the lakeside greenway in the community. When they came back, she accompanied her daughter to sleep, then spent time checking the shop's accounts and community messages to prepare for the next day's work.

events.name: Checked the vehicle in the early morning and drove alone to Quanzhou.
events.description: At 6:30 in the morning, after a simple breakfast, Song Yajing changed into a black professional suit. She checked the fuel level of the family car (sufficient), set the navigation route on the center console (directly along the Shenhai Expressway to Licheng District, Quanzhou), and placed a bottle of water, a bag of snacks, and a paper Quanzhou map in the back seat as emergency backups. She kissed the forehead of Xuanxuan, who was still asleep, said 'I'm leaving' to her husband, then drove out of the residential compound alone and merged into the sparse weekend morning traffic. The scenery along the way gradually changed from tall city buildings to the countryside of southern Fujian, and her mood was calm and solemn. At 8:30 in the morning, she arrived at the public parking lot near the church in Licheng District, Quanzhou, parked, and walked to the church.

events.name: Attended the farewell Mass and prayed in silence.
events.description: At 9:00 in the morning, Song Yajing pushed open the church door, and the familiar scents of old and new wood and candle smoke rushed toward her. There were already twenty or thirty relatives and friends seated inside. She walked in softly and saw Wu Xiaoli and several relatives sitting in the front row from a distance. Instead of going over to greet them, she chose to sit quietly in a seat a few rows back. When the Mass began, Father Wang presided over the liturgy, and the choir's singing echoed beneath the dome. Song Yajing folded her hands and bowed her head, praying for the soul of the departed and offering a blessing for her father, who had cared for his daughter while he was alive. She participated quietly throughout, using her silent presence as the greatest support.

events.name: Hug Wu Xiaoli and provide emotional support
events.description: After the memorial service ended, relatives and friends stepped forward one by one to shake hands with the family. Song Yajing waited until the crowd had drifted away a little before she walked up to Wu Xiaoli. The moment their eyes met, she saw her old classmate's reddened, swollen eyes and the strength she was trying hard to hold back. Song Yajing said nothing, just opened her arms and gave her a long, firm hug. The hug lasted several seconds. Then she took a small Virgin Mary card from her bag and gently pressed it into Xiaoli's palm, whispering, 'I'm here whenever you need me, just like in our first year of high school when you listened to me cry on the stairway for a whole afternoon. Today I'll stay with you.' Wu Xiaoli's eyes glistened with tears. She squeezed the card tightly and nodded.

events.name: Accompany and sort out the deceased's belongings
events.description: After the other relatives and classmates had gradually left, Song Yajing accompanied Wu Xiaoli back to the Wu family's old home deep in a lane in Licheng District. The living room held photos of her late father and clothes and books that needed sorting. Song Yajing rolled up her sleeves and helped sort them—what could be donated, what should be kept for relatives as mementos, and what old items should be discarded. The two chatted sporadically as they sorted, talking about the books her father had loved and the Nanyin music he had enjoyed, occasionally falling into silence. When Wu Xiaoli came across an old sweater of her father's, she finally couldn't hold it in and burst out crying. Song Yajing put down what she was doing, moved over, and put her arm around her shoulder, letting her cry for a long time. Only at 2 p.m. did she say goodbye to Xiaoli, promising to stay in touch.

events.name: Called my father on the way back and wrote down my reflections.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Song Yajing set out from Quanzhou and drove back to Xiamen along the same route. About an hour later, she pulled into the Puli Service Area on the Shenhai Expressway and stopped to rest. Sitting on a bench in the service area, she felt the gentle autumn sunshine. She took out her phone and called her father, Song Minghui. “Dad, I just came back from the funeral of a classmate's father, and I miss you.” Her voice was a little hoarse. On the other end, her father paused, then said gently, “I'm fine. Your mother and I are both well. Your back hasn't fully recovered yet, so drive carefully.” Song Yajing urged her father to make sure he got a regular physical checkup every year and not to brush it off as he used to. Her father laughed and said, “Okay, I promise you. I'll go after the first lunar month. Also, your mother and I are always waiting for you to come home, and bring Xuanxuan too.” Before hanging up, she added, “This Spring Festival, Xuanxuan and I will stay for a few more days.” After the call, she sat for a while and wrote in her phone memo: “Today I deeply realized that 'the child wants to care for a parent who is no longer there' is not just an old saying — it really can become too late. From now on, I will return to Quanzhou at least once a quarter, even if it's just to have a meal with them.”

events.name: In the evening, we had our first official family walk, and I accompanied my daughter to sleep.
events.description: By the time she got home in Xiamen in the evening, Chen Zhiqiang had already prepared dinner (two dishes and a soup). After eating, Song Yajing announced, "Come on, let's go for a walk!" This was the first implementation of the family's daily walking plan agreed upon by the couple the previous night. The three put on their sports shoes and set off from home on Hubin South Road, walking slowly along the lakefront greenway outside the residential area that Chen Zhiqiang had planned in advance. Xuanxuan would run ahead to pick up fallen leaves one moment, then hold her father's hand to cross the road safely the next. Song Yajing walked behind, watching her husband and daughter from behind, feeling her lower back gradually relax during the slow walk. Half an hour later, they returned home. She helped her daughter wash up, read her a bedtime story, and only quietly left the children's room after Xuanxuan had fallen into a deep sleep. In the final half hour, she sat alone on the living room sofa, opened her laptop, quickly checked the store's daily sales records and community group messages, and noted in her diary app the only small joy of the day: "Today I bade farewell to one father and called another. First day of walking, the whole family is together."

She wrote down the adjustment plan in her memo.
